A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ExtraCare research. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: V1 reports original eICU and OCHIN prediction experiments, component ablations, representation probes and patient-level explanation analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds explanation comparisons, LLM and human evaluations, residual-masking experiments and threshold sensitivity results.

M1.justification: The encoder, sparse autoencoder, dictionary-induced projection, losses and prediction procedure remain unchanged, as does Algorithm 1. Residual masking in Appendix K is an evaluation intervention, not a revision of the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use eICU and OCHIN for diagnosis and heart-failure prediction, retaining the geographic, temporal and five specialty-facility transfer settings. The added explanation assessments and ablations reuse the existing OCHIN facility setting.

E2.justification: V2 introduces an evaluated explanation-comparison suite comprising SHAP, Integrated Gradients and regular SAE in Section 4.4 and Figure 3. Regular SAE also becomes the comparator in the paired judge study. The existing predictive baseline sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 4.4 and Appendix J.5 add matched candidate-code budgets, patient-relevance and facility-specificity anchors, LAD/DAD/QCE metrics, and anonymized randomized explanation judging: 300 LLM cases and 25 cases assessed by two medically trained humans. Appendix K adds fixed-head residual masking and a threshold sweep. Existing prediction protocols are retained.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's component ablations, probes and patient cases, v2 tests explanation grounding against external anchors and judge preferences. Appendix K adds interventions testing whether residual information affects predictions, code-level masking examples, and sensitivity to the explanation threshold.

E5.justification: The retained prediction tables continue reporting the same means and standard errors. V2 adds no seed counts, repeated-run information, confidence intervals, significance tests or judge-agreement estimates; the new evaluation results are point estimates.

E6.justification: Existing prediction and probe values remain unchanged. New Figure 3 reports ExtraCare versus SAE LAD of 47% versus 36%, DAD of 42% versus 40%, and QCE of 32% versus 37%. Table 3 reports 68% LLM and 64% human preference for ExtraCare over SAE. Appendix K adds masking and threshold results, including Mental Health R@5 falling from 79.9 to 66.3 when the residual is masked.

T1.justification: The original assumptions, projection definitions, proposition, lemma and proofs are retained. Appendix J.5 adds mathematical definitions for patient relevance, facility specificity and LAD/DAD/QCE in Equations 18–22, extending the formal evaluation framework without changing the method's theory.

C1.justification: The abstract and introductory contributions retain their original scope. V2 adds RQ3 and a conclusion claim that patient/facility anchors and judge evaluations establish stronger explanation-axis separation and clearer explanations than standard explanation baselines.

C2.justification: V2 interprets the new comparisons as support for label-domain factorization beyond sparsity alone. Appendix K argues that the residual is actively used in facility-sensitive predictions and discusses threshold-dependent calibration. Appendix J.5 specifically limits its anchors and judging rubric to grounding and auditability rather than causal correctness.

D1.justification: Appendix I.2 adds a code-repository pointer. Appendix J.5 documents attribution targets, candidate-code ranking and truncation, and judging rubrics. Existing architecture, hyperparameters, optimizer, training schedule and hardware disclosures remain unchanged; the repository's actual availability is not established by the PDFs.

R1.justification: V2 adds references supporting SHAP/IG comparisons, recent clinical interpretability work and the information-theoretic discussion, and replaces the OCHIN source citations. The overall research positioning remains stable. BUA's bibliographic update and the retitled Hu domain-discovery work do not represent new comparison methods.

P1.justification: V2 makes local grammar edits, updates the running title, corresponding author and acknowledgments, and inserts RQ3, Section 4.4, Appendix J.5 and Appendix K. The existing narrative and section order are largely preserved rather than extensively rewritten.

P2.justification: V2 substantially expands the visual presentation of explanation validation through Figures 3 and 5 and Tables 3, 9 and 10. Figure 1 is redrawn, and Table 2 switches runner-up highlighting from blue text to gray shading. Existing result displays are retained, with several relocated or renumbered.

improvement.justification: V1's central transparency claim relied mainly on illustrative patient cases and representation probes. V2 addresses that validation gap with explanation comparators, patient-record and prevalence anchors, randomized anonymized judgments, and functional residual and threshold tests in Section 4.4 and Appendices J.5–K. These materially strengthen support for the paper's central contribution. The small human study and missing uncertainty estimates and judge-model details still limit conclusiveness.
